instagram_note: Primary handle per the business's own GlossGenius page (instagram_url field) and Facebook. A second handle, @japaneseheadspagnv, was also checked via the Instagram API this session: its full_name resolves to 'Luxe Flo Spa' and its bio links to linktr.ee/luxeflospagnv, confirming it is the SAME business's head-spa-specific promotional sub-account (359 followers, 52 posts), not a different business. @luxeflospa (main handle) itself returned a blocked/rate-limited response on both attempts this session (max-2-attempts rule reached), so its own feed could not be pulled directly, but it is confirmed as the business's primary handle from first-party sources (GlossGenius, Facebook cross-reference).
website_check: luxeflospa.com and 5 obvious variants (luxeflospagainesville.com, luxeflospallc.com, luxe-flo-spa.com, theluxeflospa.com, luxeflospa.net, luxeflospa.co) all fail to resolve at the DNS/connection level (confirmed via curl through the network proxy, cross-checked against known-good domains resolving fine in the same session, ruling out a proxy issue). The business's own GlossGenius page explicitly sets website_url to null in its own data, and its About page lists only Facebook, Instagram and Yelp as external links. No dedicated domain found anywhere in Fresha, Yelp search results, or Google search results. Confirmed has_own_site: false.

about: Luxe Flo Spa is the Gainesville, FL studio of Chanelle Gallardo, a holistic esthetician and brow specialist. She treats acne, sun damage and anti-aging, and also offers massage, waxing, tinting, lash and Japanese head spa services. The business is woman-owned (self-declared feature on its Fresha/Google listing), created in January 2023, and works with a small team including Katie (head spa/massage) and Natalia.

reviews_note: First 5 quotes pulled live this session directly from Fresha's GraphQL-backed reviews payload embedded in the location page (props.pageProps.data.location.reviews, totalCount 15, all rating 5), with real first-name + last-initial attribution matching the format used across prior builds. 2 additional quotes (Jessica H., Jamie Z.) were pulled from real client-testimonial graphics posted to the business's own Instagram feed (@luxeflospa), which quote named clients verbatim; these 2 are used only in this data.json for extra corroboration and were not placed on-site since the site already had 3 clean, on-brand testimonial slots filled from the verified Fresha API data. The single unattributed Fresha-comment fragment mentioned in the task brief ('Chanelle is amazing, patient and kind', re: a brow service) was in fact traceable to a named reviewer, Pam B., in the same Fresha reviews payload, resolving that ambiguity.
language_source: All sourced text (GlossGenius about copy, Fresha reviews and descriptions, Instagram captions) is in English. Gainesville, FL is an English-language market with no Spanish-language signal found anywhere in the business's own content.
review_count_note: Not fully resolved to a single authoritative number, presented honestly: (1) localheadspa.com, a Google Business Profile aggregator, shows 'Luxe Flo Spa is a head spa in Gainesville, FL with 5 stars from 57 reviews' on a direct live fetch this session, and the same page independently displays a matching Google Place ID (ChIJ6QoHK7-76IgR8T08lQx1i2U) and two Google-Business-Profile-sourced attributes (LGBTQ+ friendly, safe space for transgender guests), which is reasonably strong circumstantial evidence the 57 figure reflects real Google Maps data, not a fabricated number. However, a separate WebSearch of the same source's cached/indexed snapshot showed 49 reviews (an older crawl), confirming the count is live and growing rather than genuinely inconsistent between two different sources. (2) Yelp, which would have been the ideal independent second source, returned HTTP 403 (bot-blocked) on direct fetch this session, so its review count could not be independently cross-checked. (3) Facebook's page also blocked/redirected on fetch. (4) Fresha's OWN review pool (a smaller, separate platform-specific count, not Google) shows exactly 15 reviews, all 5-star, verified via Fresha's own API payload; this is used on-site as its own clearly-labeled 'reviews on Fresha' figure with a working link to the live 15-review page, rather than being conflated with the Google-sourced 57. Net confidence: MEDIUM on 57 as the Google figure (one strong circumstantial source, live-fetched, not independently corroborated by a second live source); HIGH confidence on 15 as the Fresha figure (directly verified API data with a working public link). Both figures are used transparently on-site, each correctly labeled to its actual platform.

images.source: Instagram main handle (@luxeflospa) API calls were blocked/rate-limited on both attempts this session (max-2-attempts rule reached: first returned a 400 'asset deleted' schema error, second returned a 401 rate-limit message), so its feed photos could not be pulled directly. The related @japaneseheadspagnv account (confirmed same business, see instagram_note) WAS accessible and yielded 9 real photos, but all 9 turned out to be marketing graphics with text overlays and taglines (e.g. 'SEE THE DIFFERENCE BEYOND CLEAN', client-quote cards) rather than clean photography, so none were usable in the gallery per the no-text-overlay rule; they were used only to source real named review quotes and the business's own logo (cropped from a clean solid-background portion of one graphic, not fabricated). The real usable photography came from Fresha's location page media library (6 professional venue photos: 2 treatment rooms, storefront entrance, 2 lounge/waiting areas, 1 esthetician station) and from a Google Business Profile portrait photo of the owner surfaced via localheadspa.com (lh3.googleusercontent.com), used only as a small avatar per the no-selfies-in-gallery rule.

images.curation_note: 7 real, verified photos (6 professional venue photos of the actual studio + 1 real owner portrait used only as a small avatar) plus 1 real cropped logo icon, all visually inspected one by one before selection. This is below the ideal 6-14 range on real distinct photography alone; per the pipeline rule 'mejor menos secciones con buenas fotos que rellenar con malas', 2 of the 6 venue photos are intentionally reused once each between the experience section and the gallery (storefront and lounge) rather than padding the gallery with the marketing-graphic or stock images that were discarded. No selfies, no closed-eyes mid-procedure shots, no clutter and no text-overlay screenshots appear in the final gallery.

brand_vibe: The business's own Instagram/marketing graphics use a droplet-and-leaf gold-and-green logo mark on dark backdrops ('LUXE FLO SPA / SKINCARE - MASSAGE - JAPANESE HEAD SPA'), but the real, verified interior photos (Fresha venue gallery) show a light, airy studio: cream walls, warm wood floors, deep forest-green accent walls and furniture, and soft blush/cream linens. Given the design system's preference for deriving the palette from the REAL interior photography over marketing-graphic styling, a light base (matching the actual studio's cream/wood tones) with a deep forest-green primary accent (matching the physical accent walls and dresser) and a warm antique-gold secondary accent (matching the real logo's gold) was chosen: distinct, on-brand, and not yet used in this exact combination.
